That screen flicker is painful to watch, though. :)
screen flicker is still a thing, they correct it post-prepossessing these days. Watch the small print in adverts, it says simulated screen images.

It's due to the refresh rates of monitors not matching up with the shutter speed of the camcorder, which is often set to record at the framerates for broadcast television which is about 24 FPS. It gives the impression of rolling lines in the monitor due to so many missing frames. This isn't something you need to fix in post-production if you film it right the first time. Of course, back then such a camera would cost a small fortune - certainly beyond the budget of such programs. Today it's an easy feature set to come by.

The actual way to fix this is to use the syncroscan feature present on some camcorders to adjust the shutter speed to 1/60th of a second (to match a 60Hz refresh rate), and to time the captures with the screen updates. The higher the refresh rate of the monitor, the faster the shutter speed needs to be to compensate.
